header.subtitle: why Redis answers before Postgres wakes up

buffer.label: THE SCAN
buffer.sub: reads every row to find one

payloads: the very same user row was read straight back off the disk on every single request even though not one byte of it had actually changed since nine this morning
redis keeps that one row sitting right there in memory so the second request never even reaches the database and comes back before the disk has been asked at all

captions.text: why is the same query slow every time?
the disk re-read a row that never changed.
redis answers from memory, not from disk.
the first request still pays full price.
